headline: Three Astros homers hold off Phillies rally, 6-5
recap: Houston built an early lead on three home runs and held off a late Phillies rally, winning 6-5 at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday. Christian Walker hit a three-run homer in the top of the second, and Jeremy Peña's double later that inning scored Cam Smith to make it 4-0. Smith added a solo home run in the fourth to push Houston's lead to 5-0. Andrew Painter (3-9) was charged with all five runs on 10 hits over five innings and took the loss.

The Phillies got on the board in the sixth when Kyle Schwarber's single scored Justin Crawford, and Trea Turner followed with a two-run homer to cut the deficit to 5-3. Daulton Varsho answered with a solo homer for Houston in the top of the seventh. Brandon Marsh's double drove in Alec Bohm in the bottom of the seventh to make it 6-4, and Edmundo Sosa's double scored Bryson Stott in the ninth, but Philadelphia could not complete the comeback. Hayden Wesneski (5-1) picked up the win, and Josh Hader worked around a run in the ninth for his 24th save.

The loss dropped the Phillies to 81-64, second in the NL East, 4.0 games behind the division-leading Braves (85-60). Philadelphia and Houston continue their series Wednesday at Citizens Bank Park, with first pitch scheduled for 6:40 PM ET. Cristopher Sánchez is set to start for the Phillies opposite Houston's Hunter Brown. DraftKings has the Phillies favored at -167 on the moneyline, with Philadelphia at -1.5 on the run line (+128).
